function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. function.name: read_output

function.name: search_output

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run

'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: run

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text

Found the bug: in group_as's valid_next (sqlparse/engine/grouping.py), the check order is `not imt(token, t=ttypes) and token is not None`. Since Python evaluates left-to-right, `imt(token, ...)` gets called even when `token` is None (i.e., there's no token after AS), and `imt` does `token.ttype in t`, raising `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ttype'`. This differs from every other `valid_next`/`valid_prev` helper in the file, which check `token is not None` first. I'll swap the order and then run the test suite to confirm the fix.

Found the bug: in group_as's valid_next (sqlparse/engine/grouping.py), the check order is `not imt(token, t=ttypes) and token is not None`. Since Python evaluates left-to-right, `imt(token, ...)` gets called even when `token` is None (i.e., there's no token after AS), and `imt` does `token.ttype in t`, raising `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ttype'`. This differs from every other `valid_next`/`valid_prev` helper in the file, which check `token is not None` first. I'll swap the order and then run the test suite to confirm the fix.

Since Python evaluates left-to-right, `imt(token, ...)` gets called even when `token` is None (i.e., there's no token after AS), and `imt` does `token.ttype in t`, raising `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ttype'`. This differs from every other `valid_next`/`valid_prev` helper in the file, which check `token is not None` first. I'll swap the order and then run the test suite to confirm the fix.

This is exactly what breaks `group_order` (sqlparse/engine/grouping.py), which calls `imt(prev_, i=sql.Identifier, t=T.Number)` where `prev_` can legitimately be None (e.g. token_prev finds no previous token) — this matches the "parse order" (8 cases) failures. The `group_as` fix I already made addresses the 'grouping identifier invalid' / 'issue284 as grouping' cases. Now hardening `imt()` itself to return False for a None token (its natural/expected behavior, consistent with how every other None-token check in the codebase treats "no match"), then verifying with manual test scripts since no local tests/ directory exists in this checkout.

Found the bug: in group_as's valid_next (sqlparse/engine/grouping.py), the check order is `not imt(token, t=ttypes) and token is not None`. Since Python evaluates left-to-right, `imt(token, ...)` gets called even when `token` is None (i.e., there's no token after AS), and `imt` does `token.ttype in t`, raising `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ttype'`. This differs from every other `valid_next`/`valid_prev` helper in the file, which check `token is not None` first. I'll swap the order and then run the test suite to confirm the fix.

Found a second, more fundamental bug: the `imt()` helper in sqlparse/utils.py does not handle a `None` token when a `t` (ttype) argument is given — it falls through to `token.ttype in t`, raising AttributeError on None. This is exactly what breaks `group_order` (sqlparse/engine/grouping.py), which calls `imt(prev_, i=sql.Identifier, t=T.Number)` where `prev_` can legitimately be None (e.g. token_prev finds no previous token) — this matches the "parse order" (8 cases) failures. The `group_as` fix I already made addresses the 'grouping identifier invalid' / 'issue284 as grouping' cases. Now hardening `imt()` itself to return False for a None token (its natural/expected behavior, consistent with how every other None-token check in the codebase treats "no match"), then verifying with manual test scripts since no local tests/ directory exists in this checkout.

A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

{"content":"Root cause found and fixed.

The regression was introduced by two related bugs that both manifest as `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ttype'`:

1. `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`, `group_as()`'s `valid_next`:
   ```python
   return not imt(token, t=ttypes) and token is not None
   ```
   This calls `imt()` (which does `token.ttype in t`) on `token` *before* checking it isn't `None`. When `AS` appears at the end of a token stream (issue284 case), `token` is `None` and this crashes. Fixed by reordering to check `token is not None` first (matching every other `valid_prev`/`valid_next` helper in the file):
   ```python
   return token is not None and not imt(token, t=ttypes)
   ```

2. `sqlparse/utils.py`'s shared `imt()` helper itself was not None-safe: when called with a `t=` (ttype) argument and `token is None`, it fell through to `token.ttype in t` and crashed. Many call sites throughout `grouping.py` legitimately pass a possibly-`None` token (e.g. `group_order`'s `imt(prev_, i=sql.Identifier, t=T.Number)` where `prev_` comes from `token_prev` and can be `None`; `group_period`, `group_over`, `group_comparison`, `group_identifier_list`, `group_operator`, `group_arrays` similarly pass results of `token_next`/`token_prev` that can be `None`). This explains the "parse order" (8 cases) and "grouping identifier invalid" failures. Fixed by adding an explicit None-guard at the top of `imt()`:
   ```python
   if token is None:
       return False
   ```

Root cause found and fixed.

The regression was introduced by two related bugs that both manifest as `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ttype'`:

1. `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`, `group_as()`'s `valid_next`:
   ```python
   return not imt(token, t=ttypes) and token is not None
   ```
   This calls `imt()` (which does `token.ttype in t`) on `token` *before* checking it isn't `None`. When `AS` appears at the end of a token stream (issue284 case), `token` is `None` and this crashes. Fixed by reordering to check `token is not None` first (matching every other `valid_prev`/`valid_next` helper in the file):
   ```python
   return token is not None and not imt(token, t=ttypes)
   ```

2. `sqlparse/utils.py`'s shared `imt()` helper itself was not None-safe: when called with a `t=` (ttype) argument and `token is None`, it fell through to `token.ttype in t` and crashed. Many call sites throughout `grouping.py` legitimately pass a possibly-`None` token (e.g. `group_order`'s `imt(prev_, i=sql.Identifier, t=T.Number)` where `prev_` comes from `token_prev` and can be `None`; `group_period`, `group_over`, `group_comparison`, `group_identifier_list`, `group_operator`, `group_arrays` similarly pass results of `token_next`/`token_prev` that can be `None`). This explains the "parse order" (8 cases) and "grouping identifier invalid" failures. Fixed by adding an explicit None-guard at the top of `imt()`:
   ```python
   if token is None:
       return False
   ```

Both changes are minimal, defensive, and consistent with the None-handling conventions already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. `_token_matching` returning `(None, None)`, and other `valid_prev`/`valid_next` closures checking `token is not None` first).

Verified with manual smoke tests (no local `tests/` directory exists in this checkout, so hidden upstream tests will validate fully): `foo AS`, `SELECT foo AS`, `SELECT * FROM foo ORDER BY 1 DESC`, `foo, bar`, and `ORDER BY` alone all parse without error and produce correctly grouped tokens (e.g. `Identifier '1 DESC'`, `IdentifierList 'foo, bar'`), confirming the AttributeError is gone and grouping behavior is correct.

message.content:
Root cause found and fixed.

The regression was introduced by two related bugs that both manifest as `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ttype'`:

1. `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`, `group_as()`'s `valid_next`:
   ```python
   return not imt(token, t=ttypes) and token is not None
   ```
   This calls `imt()` (which does `token.ttype in t`) on `token` *before* checking it isn't `None`. When `AS` appears at the end of a token stream (issue284 case), `token` is `None` and this crashes. Fixed by reordering to check `token is not None` first (matching every other `valid_prev`/`valid_next` helper in the file):
   ```python
   return token is not None and not imt(token, t=ttypes)
   ```

2. `sqlparse/utils.py`'s shared `imt()` helper itself was not None-safe: when called with a `t=` (ttype) argument and `token is None`, it fell through to `token.ttype in t` and crashed. Many call sites throughout `grouping.py` legitimately pass a possibly-`None` token (e.g. `group_order`'s `imt(prev_, i=sql.Identifier, t=T.Number)` where `prev_` comes from `token_prev` and can be `None`; `group_period`, `group_over`, `group_comparison`, `group_identifier_list`, `group_operator`, `group_arrays` similarly pass results of `token_next`/`token_prev` that can be `None`). This explains the "parse order" (8 cases) and "grouping identifier invalid" failures. Fixed by adding an explicit None-guard at the top of `imt()`:
   ```python
   if token is None:
       return False
   ```

Both changes are minimal, defensive, and consistent with the None-handling conventions already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. `_token_matching` returning `(None, None)`, and other `valid_prev`/`valid_next` closures checking `token is not None` first).

Verified with manual smoke tests (no local `tests/` directory exists in this checkout, so hidden upstream tests will validate fully): `foo AS`, `SELECT foo AS`, `SELECT * FROM foo ORDER BY 1 DESC`, `foo, bar`, and `ORDER BY` alone all parse without error and produce correctly grouped tokens (e.g. `Identifier '1 DESC'`, `IdentifierList 'foo, bar'`), confirming the AttributeError is gone and grouping behavior is correct.
